## AC.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The banner-✕ / send-FAB region trap (AB.A0.5) re-manifested and cost one send:**
   the leg-1 refusal banner was still up when leg 3's first send tap fired at
   (960,1450) — the tap hit the banner's ✕ (rendered (810,1220) → device ≈(948,1464)),
   the banner dismissed, the draft survived, no wire. Recipe sharpened: **before every
   send tap, CHECK FOR A BANNER in the pre-send screenshot** — its ✕ shares the FAB's
   region and the layout re-flows on dismissal; the leg-3 re-tap one banner-cycle later
   landed cleanly.
2. **The attachment dropdown's Photo row is IME-CLIPPED when the keyboard is open:**
   with the IME up, the + dropdown renders at its anchored height and Photo sits under
   the IME's top edge (partially visible). BACK with the dropdown open closes the
   DROPDOWN (not the IME — the pass-23 BACK-pops-route note generalizes to dropdowns);
   BACK with the dropdown closed dismisses the IME; with NO IME the composer drops to
   full height (Add attachment at (123,2184) per the AX — honest at full-height layout)
   and the dropdown renders ALL rows (Mention a file / Sketch / Photo / Attach a file /
   Take photo / Dictate). Recipe: neutral-tap → BACK (IME) → + → Photo.
3. **The keycode table correction: keyevent 43 is O, not T** (the first-leg attempt
   produced `/oarget`): keycode = 29 + (letter − A); T = 48, R = 46, C = 31, G = 35,
   P = 44 (the pass-24/25 examples stand). Also: tapping (540,1900) while the IME is
   open and the composer sits higher types an IME key (`g`) — tap the composer's
   ACTUAL rendered position, never a remembered coordinate.
4. **The photo picker keeps tile selections across dismiss/reopen:** a tap in the
   Dismiss region while the grid is up can SELECT a tile — this pass's picker session
   staged TWO chips (a stray `86.png (229.1 KB)` + the target `119.png (74 B)`, the
   MediaStore-id rename pattern pass 25 recorded). Remove stray chips before the send
   (the per-chip Remove affordance at the chip row's right edge).
5. **The content query projection is single-column per flag on API 36:**
   `content query --uri … --projection _id,_display_name` fails with "Invalid column";
   query bare and grep the Row output for `_display_name`/`_id` (rig-p26.png = id 119).
6. The residue-draft `install -r` survival folklore continues, but the pass-25 plan
   draft did NOT survive this pass's install (the composer was EMPTY at first open) —
   the draft row survived earlier passes as the same-process restore; a fresh process
   restored nothing because the pass-25 draft was cleared post-leg. No pattern change,
   just the observed variance.

## AD.A0 — rig learnings

1. **Per-char `input text` is THE reliable typing recipe on this IME** — every other
   method failed deterministically this pass: keyevent-per-letter garbled
   (`/goal resume` typed as `/obl resume`: the G after keyevent-76 dropped AND the A
   landed as B — a keycode-adjacent shift beyond the pass-25/26 drop note); one-chunk
   `input text 'goal%sresume'` INTERLEAVED (`/goaesumel` — the known interleave); and
   the first chunk following fresh field focus drops its first char
   (`input text '/c'` after keyevent-76 landed only `/`). Per-char single-char
   `input text` calls with ~300 ms sleeps landed 11/11 (`/goal resume`) and 7/8
   (only the fresh-focus first char of `/compact` dropped — repaired by cursor math,
   see 2).
2. **The slash-command menu INTERCEPTS keyevents while open:** with the Commands
   dropdown up, MOVE_END/DEL went nowhere and a full retype no-op'd (the draft
   unchanged across a clear+retype attempt); BACK closes the DROPDOWN (AC.A0.2 again)
   and returns the keyevents to the field. Deterministic repair for a garbled draft:
   single DEL / RIGHT / insert with the cursor — this pass inserted the missing `c`
   after `/` exactly that way (`/ompact` → DEL the stray leading c → RIGHT past the
   slash → `input text 'c'` → `/compact`).
3. **Re-dump before EVERY composer interaction:** the chip row and the Commands menu

## AE.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The composer + DropdownMenu renders INVISIBLY to BOTH `screencap` AND
   `uiautomator dump`** on this build (four screenshots s06/s08/s09/s11 show the
   conversation with no menu; the dump has no menu nodes) while TAPS still land on it
   (one blind tap hit "Sketch" and opened the Sketch dialog — the calibration event).
   The slash Commands dropdown, by contrast, renders normally in both (s01). The
   deterministic recipe: **`dumpsys window windows` gives the popup's frame**
   (this pass: `frame=[61,1170][369,2006]` = 836 px = 6 rows × 132 px (48 dp @ 2.75×)
   + padding; rows top→bottom in code order mention/sketch/photo/doc/camera/voice →
   doc row center y = 1170 + 22 + 3.5×132 ≈ 1654 — the tap landed File exactly).
2. **The second BACK pops the route again** (pass 23's learning re-manifested): BACK 1
   closed the IME, BACK 2 popped the conversation to Tasks home. One BACK per surface;
   re-dump after each.
3. **Screenshot taps need NO scale correction on this rig** — the PNG is full-res
   1080×2340 (`sips -g pixelWidth` verified); the ~17 % offsets recorded in earlier
   passes are the READ-TOOL's preview scale, not the PNG. Estimate in preview pixels
   → multiply by 1080/891 (x) and 2340/2000 (y) when reading coordinates off the
   rendered preview.
4. **The mock's request `id=` counter is PER-CONNECTION** — the app made 3 connections
   this pass (initial + 2 reconnects) and each restarts at `helloConversationV4
   (id=3)`; the relay log therefore shows id sequences 1..28, 3..14, 3..33. Do not
   read a dropping id as a relay restart — grep `MOCKZCODE_READY` (1) and the process
   start time instead.
5. **Per-word chunks of `input text` are adequate for plain-text drafts** ("stop leg
   probe" landed exact; "notes for review" lost one char — the trailing `w` landed
   mid-cursor as `reviwe`, left verbatim and recorded; the dump's
   `resource-id="composer_field"` EditText node is the arbiter for the draft).
6. **DocumentsUI (the OpenDocument target) is fully dump-drivable** even when its
   pixels lag blank under swiftshader (w13 carried the whole Recent list; the
   MediaStore-scanned file's row tapped by dump bounds).

   — the first attempt (gen1, 4 s chunks ⇒ a 16 s window) MISSED: the Remove tap was
   composed in a separate tool call after a Read roundtrip, and the transaction
   completed (begin → 4 chunks → commit, abort ×0) before the tap landed. The fix:
   **the entire tile-tap → Remove → resurrection sequence must run inside ONE bash
   command** (sleeps only, no Read roundtrips), and 15 s/chunk (a 60 s window) makes
   even that comfortable. The pass-30 "racy without a longer arm" note is confirmed
   and sharpened.

   gap outlasted the app's ladder — five reconnect attempts timed out (relay-51..55,
   10 s each) and the app walked to **DEGRADED** ("Disconnected" header + the

upload coroutine — the aborted transaction resurrects the removed chip. Mechanism
pins: `removeUpload` (`Ports.kt:1154-1167`) aborts the wire + filters the list but

user-removed set). Pin: a harness asserting remove-during-upload → the chip stays
gone + the abort fires. The desktop's own mid-upload remove behavior is UNCENSUSED

## AI.D — the desktop census: remove is FINAL on the desktop (static, asar `ec475e6e…`)

The fix-round static item from AH.D, now closed. The desktop composer
(`styles-DNV2PY7o.js`, the attachment plane `ume`/`W8t`/`e5t`) implements THREE
mechanisms the phone's port lacks:

1. **Per-chip AbortController**: every upload gets `i=new AbortController` keyed
   `scopeKey\0attachmentId` in a ref map (`v.current`); the V4 upload loop
   (`ume`) checks `Dm(r.signal)` BEFORE EVERY chunk (pre-flight throw
   AbortError) — mid-flight removal stops the next chunk from ever being SENT.
2. **Staleness-guarded callbacks**: the onProgress handler and the
   success/failure completion paths ALL check `v.current.get(r)!==i` (the
   controller still registered for THIS attachment) — a removed chip's late chunk
   answers are dropped instead of re-adding it; the catch path additionally
   checks `i.signal.aborted`.
3. **Transfer-service cancel**: remove (`ce` callback) aborts the controller,
   deletes the map entry, dequeues pending work, cancels timers, and calls
   `transferService.cancel(operationId)` for staged/uploading/committing chips —
   plus a bulk-unmount sweep (`ue`) doing the same for every chip.

**The desktop's remove is final in every state.** The phone's port
(`Ports.kt:1154-1167` + the unconditional upserts `:1112-1115`/`:1129-1137`)
implements none of the three — F-P31-A's fix shape gains the desktop-parity pin:
track per-uploadId Jobs (the phone's analogue of the controller map), cancel in
`removeUpload`, and guard both re-add upserts on the staleness/user-removed set
(the direct analogue of `v.current.get(r)!==i`).

## AJ.A0 — rig learnings

1. **`am start` works where `monkey -p … -c LAUNCHER 1` fails**: the monkey launch died
   with `VM exiting with result code -5` (injection refused, app never started) on this
   inherited emulator; `am start -n com.zcode.android.app/.MainActivity` (the
   resolve-activity brief form) started it first try. The launcher recipe gains the
   am-start fallback.
2. **The initial snapshot page renders ONLY its last rows and the two SLOW drags
   (400 ms) scrolled ~0 px while the FAST fling (200 ms) scrolled normally** — the
   first dump-of-the-pass showed the row-kind block as if it were the whole timeline;
   the DB pull arbitrated (all 24 rows persisted, `conversation_rows` census 24 ✓
   incl. `futureWidget` stored under its own kind) and the second fling revealed the
   earlier rows. Lesson: after opening a conversation, FLING (fast) — and when the
   viewport looks truncated, pull the DB before concluding data loss.
3. **On-device APK digest: `run-as … cat base.apk` from the app dir returns the
   EMPTY-file md5 (d41d8cd9…)** — the relative path resolves wrong; use
   `adb shell md5sum /data/app/~~…/base.apk` (the pm path). The pass-32-era "run-as cat"
   recipe silently compared nothing.
4. **Screenshot-space vs dump-space taps bit AGAIN** (the pass-31 lesson, second
   manifestation): the Retry tap computed from the s05 screenshot (y=1251) missed;
   the re-dumped bounds (y=1464) hit first tap. Dump bounds remain the only tap
   authority.
5. The uiautomator dump missed NOTHING this pass (no ghost frames — the pass-32
   ghost was variance, not trend).

## AJ.G — leg F: the artifact preview card's Open affordance is DEAD and SILENT — NEW F-P33-A (02:26 gen1 / 02:34 gen2)

**Stage-2 (gen1, the seeded-bytes card `rig-p33-report.html`)**: tap `Open externally`
(959,1344) → the download SUCCEEDS (the file lands at
`/data/data/com.zcode.android.app/cache/downloads/rig-p33-report.html`) →
`FileProvider.getUriForFile` THROWS:

```
02:26:58.598 [WARN] files.share :: IllegalArgumentException: Failed to find configured root that contains /data/data/com.zcode.android.app/cache/downloads/rig-p3…
02:26:58.606 [WARN] preview.open :: IllegalArgumentException: Failed to find configured root that contains /data/data/com.zcode.android.app/ca…
```

and s09 shows **NO user face** — the frame is pixel-identical before/after the tap.

**Stage-1 (gen2, the openable-but-unserved card `rig-p33-missing.html`, commit
`2e46a172`)**: the card renders identically (known extension) but the ref is never
seeded → `file.readFileRange refused: fault.file.notFound` →
`filesport.download :: TransportFailure` → `preview.open :: download failed:
fault.file.notFound` — and s11 again shows **NO user face**.

**The mechanism, pinned both ends**: the FilesPort.download target is
`File(appContext.cacheDir, "downloads")` (`AppContainer.kt:258`), but the FileProvider
manifest config `app/src/main/res/xml/file_paths.xml` declares ONLY
`<cache-path name="shared" path="shared/" />` and `<cache-path name="updates" path="updates/" />`
— NO root covers `cache/downloads/`, so `getUriForFile` IAEs for EVERY downloaded
artifact. `ZCodeApp.kt:1106-1133`'s failure branches are both log-only: the
download-null branch (:1110-1113) `container.log.warn("preview.open", "download failed…")`,
and the launch-failure else (:1130-1132) — G57's typed no-viewer notice matches ONLY
`isNoViewerActivityLaunch(e)` (ActivityNotFoundException-class), never this IAE. The
card renders, the button fires, the wire works, the file downloads, and the user gets
nothing — the F-P0-C silent-family shape on the preview-card plane.

**Never live-driven before**: zero artifact-row/artifact-open receipts exist in the
pass0 series (33 passes); the I2.8/G28/G57 static pins covered the RENDER and the
no-viewer fallback, not the handoff path. **Fix shape**: add
`<cache-path name="downloads" path="downloads/" />` to file_paths.xml (stage-2 — one
line) + a typed notice on the download-null branch (stage-1 — the N-BR-1/N-BS-1 notice
plane); pins: a Robolectric `getUriForFile` harness over a cache/downloads file + a
harness asserting the typed notice on `result == null`.

## AK.A0 — rig learnings

1. **Drag-start position decides whether the timeline scrolls AT ALL**: vertical drags
   STARTED ON A TOOL CARD are silently swallowed (six consecutive flings + slow drags
   moved 0 px — pixel-identical frames), while the SAME gesture started in the ~40 px
   INTER-CARD GAP scrolls normally. The pass-33 "fling beats drag" lesson was this same
   variance mis-attributed: gesture ORIGIN, not velocity, is the discriminator. When a
   conversation is wedged: tap the Jump-to-latest FAB (verified working throughout —
   input is alive, only card-originated drags die), then gap-drag.
2. **The a11y content-desc on a collapsed group reads "expand", on an expanded group
   "collapse"** — the dump is a reliable expand-state arbiter without screenshots.
3. `input swipe` gestures aimed at dialog buttons keep missing after an IME toggle
   (the dialog reflows when the keyboard hides — the pass-26 lesson, third bite):
   BACK to drop the IME FIRST, re-dump, THEN tap the fresh bounds.
4. The retried-reply row (the mock's retryTurn append) carries `ROW_ACTIONS_ASSISTANT`
   → its rail renders TEXT buttons Like/Dislike/Fork/Retry — the seeded base rows have
   no `actions` and render the icon-only 👍👎 rail (the flag-gating face, s06).
5. The fork child session seeds IDENTICALLY (every arm's snapshot is per-session) —
   driving legs "inside the fork" is wire-equivalent to the parent.

## AL.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The gap-drag recipe RE-CONFIRMED and refined** (pass-34's lesson holds): a drag
   started at x=20 (the left gutter OUTSIDE the reader-width list) scrolls NOTHING;
   the true gap is the inter-item band between the pinned strip's bottom edge and the
   first row's internal header (y≈523..641 at this layout) — drags from there move
   10–13 rows each. FLINGS from the gap move LESS than slow 250 ms drags on this
   timeline (2–3 vs 10–13 rows) — the reverse of the pass-33 note; gesture ORIGIN
   decides, velocity is secondary. Reaching the top of a 320-row timeline costs ~60
   gestures either way.
2. **Find-in-conversation cannot reach unloaded rows and reported "No matches" for a
   query whose row WAS cached** ("synthetic 82" while the store held 82..401) — the
   find plane's match window vs the loaded/render window is an unexplored edge
   (not rowed; the find-jump recipe failed for THIS leg only).
3. **BACK does not close the find panel when its field is focused** (first BACK drops
   the IME) — the panel's own "Close find" content-desc button (bounds from the dump)
   is the reliable close.
4. The snapshot window carries 321 rows under MOCK_ROWS_TOTAL=400 (81..400 synthetic
   + 401 the always-on demo-markdown row) and the phone's §17.3 snapshot apply trims
   to MAX_CACHED_ROWS_PER_SESSION=320 — row 81 is EVICTED (DB min=82). The paging
   pages therefore run 32..81 / 1..31, not 31..80 / 1..30 (the self-test pins BOTH
   shapes; the phone-real one is the receipt).
5. `applyPage` (ConversationRepositoryImpl.kt:89-109) does NOT enforceBound — the
   F-37-D fix comment documents the vc52-era self-evicting no-op; the page lands
   contiguous by construction, and the gen1/gen3 DB tallies (320→370→401; end 401 =
   320+50+31) match the contract exactly.

## AM.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The relay's stdout BUFFERING fooled `grep -c` twice**: the range-call count read
   2 for ~15 minutes while the log actually held 4 (the second open's pair appeared in
   the file only after a later write flushed the buffer). Re-grep before concluding any
   call-count; counts taken mid-session are lower bounds, not facts.
2. **The find bar's per-keystroke jump CHASE**: every query change recomputes the index
   and the jump effect re-scrolls to the CURRENT first match — so typing "synthetic 83"
   through its prefixes drags the viewport through "synthetic"→row 82, "synthetic
   8"→row 88 before landing. Pass-35's visual staging failed partly on this (the view
   was never where the leg expected). Leg-order around it: stage the frame via the
   LAST non-empty prefix's first match (AM.D's "synthetic 91" shot landed row 170 with
   row 171 in-frame BY CONSTRUCTION).
3. **Composer-misdirect is the find leg's standing trap**: pass 35 typed its query into
   the COMPOSER (the draft row proves it); the find field stayed blank and conv_find_none
   renders for a blank query — indistinguishable from a real miss on a dump. ALWAYS
   verify the FIELD's text node (the field and the composer both echo the query) before
   reading the count as a finding. The N-BF-1 auto-focus fix holds at HEAD when the bar
   opens cleanly; the misdirect happens when focus lags the open.
4. The MOVE_END + N×DEL clear recipe held for both the find field and the composer
   (12-char clears); per-char `input text` held (zero drops across ~9 typed queries).

## AM.I — NEW ROW F-P36-A (P3): the open-time prefetch race + the cache trim strand a stale `hasMore=false` — the Load-earlier strip hides while head rows are cache-absent

**The receipted sequence (2/2 fresh opens raced identically — relay log lines 24/25
and 55/56, two `conversationRowsRangeV4` calls per open, ZERO strip taps):**

1. Open the conversation: hydrate from Room (the DB cache), then the snapshot applies
   (the window 82..401, trimmed to the 320 cache bound).
2. **The open-time race**: the prefetch effect (`ConversationScreen.kt:1092-1103`,
   PAGE_EDGE=12) observes `firstVisibleItemIndex=0` in the window BEFORE the tail-clamp
   effect (`:1063-1071`, `anchoredToTail=true`) moves the view to the tail — the gate
   passes and `loadOlder` fires with `beforeRowId = rows.first()`, TWICE (the second
   after the first page applies, the view still near the edge). The strip rendered
   "320 of 400" (w2) BEFORE the pages landed and was GONE by the next dump (w9).
3. The pages (e.g. 34..83, then 1..33) apply — the page-path writer sets
   **`_hasMore.value = result.hasMore`** (`ConversationViewModel.kt:295`), and the
   second page reaches the store floor so the mock honestly answers
   `hasMore = page.first > ROW_ID_FLOOR` = **false** (MockZCode.kt rowsRangePage +
   the response builder). Honest AT THAT INSTANT — the store then held 1..401.
4. **The trim strands the stale false**: `enforceBound` runs on append and
   snapshot-apply only (`ConversationRepositoryImpl.kt:73/126`; the page path is
   deliberately unbounded per F-37-D, :96), so the next snapshot/append trims the
   head back to the newest 320 — rows 1..83 EVICTED (DB arbiter: `320|84|401` at
   12:08, later `320|84..401+1001+1002` after the send; the fresh-open end state
   `403|1..401+1001..1002` pre-next-trim).
5. **The mirror never re-derives**: the ViewModel's `_hasMore` is a MIRROR of the
   manager's authoritative flow (`:145`, `port.observeHasMoreHistory`) whose only
   writer is the snapshot-path derivation (`ConversationSessionManager.kt:248`,
   `firstRowId != null && rows.first().rowId != firstRowId` — which says TRUE here);
   but a MutableStateFlow does not re-emit an UNCHANGED value, the snapshot-path
   value stayed true→true, and the page-path overwrite at :295 is therefore FINAL
   for the session. The strip gate (`hasMoreHistory && !loadingOlder && rows.
   isNotEmpty()`) hides the affordance — **81 head rows are cache-absent and
   unreachable for the life of the subscription**.
6. **The persistence boundary (receipted)**: route pop + re-entry does NOT heal
   (the subscription and ViewModel persist; no re-subscribe, no new snapshot —
   w15). A fresh process DOES heal (force-stop → re-open → the snapshot path
   re-derives → the strip returns "320 of 400" — w17, receipted live).

**Why a defect and not a race curiosity**: the user-visible state is a LIE — the
strip says "no more history" while the cache is missing 81 rows the store HAS; a
user who paged to the floor on a >320-row conversation (or merely opened one, on
this rig) loses scroll-back access until they re-open the conversation. The end
state is honest only after a re-subscribe.

**Fix shape**: re-derive after the trim — `hasMore = firstCachedRowId > windowFirstRowId`
at every enforceBound site (or re-read the manager's authoritative value at
loadOlder completion instead of trusting the page response alone). Pins: a
Robolectric/repo harness paging to the floor with total > cache bound asserting the
strip survives the post-page trim; the DB min(rowId) > window firstRowId invariant.

**Receipts**: relay `/tmp/p36/relay-g1.log` (lines 24/25 + 55/56 — the two per-open
pairs, no taps); DB pulls `/tmp/p36/db/zcode{,2,3}.db` (82..401 → 84..401+1001+1002
→ 403@1..401+1001..1002); dumps w2 (strip present) → w9-w13 (absent, incl. w13 with
find CLOSED — the state gate, not the find bar) → w15 (absent after route re-entry)
→ w17 (PRESENT after fresh process); logcat /tmp/p36/logcat.log (zero FATALs,
zero gateway.drop).

## AN.G — NEW ROW N-BT-1 (P4): the stale row-action banner renders the SWITCH-specific copy — the renderer's key→string map discards rowActionNotice's own message

**Live receipt (14:24, s14, gen3 `MOCK_CAS_STALE_TYPES=setAssistantFeedback`)**: the
stale feedback tap rendered the WARNING banner **"The session changed on the desktop
— try the switch again."** — for a LIKE tap. Mechanism:

1. `rowActionNotice`'s STALE branch (`ConversationViewModel.kt:1147`) passes the
   ROW-ACTION-correct message "The session changed on the desktop — try again." with
   the SHARED `SendNotice.Key.SESSION_CHANGED`.
2. The banner renderer resolves BY KEY (`WriteComponents.kt:1751`:
   `SESSION_CHANGED -> R.string.notice_session_changed`) and the string is
   SWITCH-specific — `notice_session_changed` = "The session changed on the desktop —
   **try the switch again.**" (features/conversation/res/strings.xml:231; the switch
   call sites :322/:337/:351 hardcode the same switch copy for their own paths).
3. The keyed render DISCARDS the per-path message (args only for ATTACHMENT_FAILED),
   so every stale ROW ACTION renders switch copy: feedback (live-receipted), and the
   same-path trio retryTurn :990 / forkAssistant :1023 / applyFileRewind :1119
   statically.

The affected population is exactly rowActionNotice's callers on the STALE outcome;
the switch paths render their own copy correctly; the queue verbs render their own
typed "Queue changed" key (pass 20/22 receipts, unaffected). The desktop recovers
stale feedback SILENTLY (the protocol chunk's stale-recoverable set `zn` =
applyFileRewind/forkAssistant/editUserQuery/retryTurn/setAssistantFeedback/
setHighspeedMetrics) — the phone warns honestly (the established N-BQ-1-family
direction, correct) but with the wrong ACTION named.

**Fix shape**: a distinct key for the row-action stale (e.g.
`ROW_ACTION_STALE` → `notice_row_action_stale` "The session changed on the desktop —
try again."), or render `notice.message` for SESSION_CHANGED when non-blank. Pins:
a harness asserting the feedback-stale banner does NOT contain "switch"; the four
rowActionNotice call sites enumerated.

**Receipts**: s14 (the banner verbatim + the rail "Like"/"Dislike" unchanged),
relay-g3.log line 12 (`MOCK: setAssistantFeedback forced stale ->
proto.staleRevision`), the grep receipts above.

## AO.A0 — rig learnings

1. **Channel verbs log on app logcat, not relay stdout** — `zcode-task.*` receipts are
   `channel.call :: <verb> begin/ok` lines in app logcat (grep `channel.call`); the
   relay stdout only logs v4/conversation calls. Re-greping the relay log for
   setTaskUnread finds NOTHING and misreads the leg as unfired.
2. **The rename dialog bit the dump-bounds trap AGAIN (~35% this layout)**: the
   AlertDialog's dump bounds put Rename at y≈1381; the screenshot-derived center was
   (770, 964) — the tap at dump bounds DISMISSED the dialog (scrim). Archive/confirm
   dialogs: screenshot-derived bounds only (the standing rule, re-learned with a
   bigger delta than the historical ~200 px).
3. **Dropdown menus anchored above bottom-screen rows re-anchor with the row** — the
   task-row menu's Pin item sat at y≈737 for BOTH task-2 positions only because the
   list didn't reflow between dumps; after every list mutation re-dump before the
   menu tap. One blind menu tap cost a dead leg (no wire, no notice — the tap hit
   the row's drag area).
4. **IME reflow moves bottom-sheet chips too**: the GroupEditorSheet's color chips sit
   at y≈1838 without the IME and y≈1574-class with it — the recolor tap hit RED twice
   (create + edit) while aiming at Blue. The visible dot-flip face is therefore
   UNRECEIPTED (red→red); the updateTaskGroupColor WIRE round-trip is receipted.
5. `input text` dropped a trailing character again ("green-to-blued") — the per-char
   recipe or MOVE_END+DEL repair stays mandatory for dialog fields.

presented as live. User impact: duplicate rows (the ghost row IS a duplicate of the
live pinned synth-task-1 minus its flags), stale timestamps, and the rows are
OPENABLE — the ghost-row tap opened the live task's conversation (AO.J). Fix shape:
prune endpoint-scoped keys absent from the connect snapshot (or sweep across keys).
Pins: a repo harness — replaceAll(keyA) then serve only keyB → keyA's rows/section
age out.

## AP.A0 — rig learnings

1. **force-stop → immediate `am start` can silently NO-OP the launch** (twice this
   pass): the intent prints "Starting…" but no process materializes (pidof empty, no
   crash trace). The recipe is `am start -W` (waits for the draw; TotalTime 13–18 s
   cold on this machine) or sleep ≥3 s between force-stop and start.
2. **Bottom-sheet dialog dumps were TRUE this layout** (the New-task sheet and the
   group editor dumped accurate bounds pre-IME), but the IME reflow lags the dump —
   after tapping a field, wait for the keyboard BEFORE dumping, or the dump returns
   the stale (unreflowed) bounds. The AO.A0.2 AlertDialog trap did not re-bit.
3. **The color-chip flip recipe that finally works**: tap the chip BEFORE touching
   the name field — no IME, no reflow, the chips sit at their dump bounds. Pass 38's
   two attempts (create + edit) lost to the IME both times because the field came
   first.
4. `input text` mangled BOTH ways in one call ("pp39-c" for "p39-create": leading
   dup + trailing drop). The MOVE_END + N×DEL + SHORT retype repair remains
   mandatory; keep payloads ≤6 chars when the exact string matters.
5. The workspace-chip taps during a cold-start connect misdirect into the
   connection-info screen (the "Connected" status row is a tap target at the same
   y-band as the early overflow). After any relaunch, dump FIRST and drive only from
   the dump.

## AQ.A0 — rig learnings

1. **Relay launcher arms AFTER the `exec` line arm NOTHING** (gen3 written by
   appending exports to the tail — the ps-eww env check caught only MOCK_GIT): the
   canonical build re-emits the exports at the file TOP before the exec line. The
   gen1 "admissibility probe" (pre-fix jar) was redundant — the jar always carries
   the arms; the launcher decides.
2. **Compose TextField text is invisible to uiautomator when the sheet reflows**
   (the branch-name field typed "rigp40" twice because the first dump showed the
   stale placeholder — the screenshot was the arbiter; pass-39's IME-lag note
   generalized: dump bounds AND text both lag the IME reflow on sheets).
3. **Dialog dump-bounds trap did not re-bit** (DiscardConfirm + PushConfirm + the
   rename AlertDialog all drove from SCREENSHOT-derived bounds; the bottom-sheet
   dumps were true pre-IME).
4. `input text` per-char remains the recipe; "DISCARD" (uppercase per-char) landed
   clean into the typed-confirm gate.
5. **FLAG_SECURE black-captures persist across screens** — the pass's own
   screenshot-protection discriminator toggle (F-P40-B's Settings-write control)
   blacked every capture until reverted; screenshot the toggle's effect before
   moving on.

## AQ.E — gen4: the typed faces → NEW ROW F-P40-C (P3) + F-P5-A stamp 2

- **MOCK_GIT_BRANCH_ISSUE** (`{"code":"switch-conflict","message":"Switching
  branches would overwrite uncommitted changes.","detail":"src/version.ts",
  "paths":["src/version.ts"]}`): Switch → `git.switchBranch ok` (the desktop-
  faithful SUCCESS-with-issues ack, didChange=false, no mutation) → **NOTHING
  renders** (s29: the pane looks exactly like the healthy state). Mechanism —
  three stacked kills: GitScreen:517 closes the BranchSheet BEFORE the async
  result lands; the close fires onDismiss (:515) which sets
  `gitBranchIssue = null`; and the only render target is
  `IssueLine` INSIDE the closed sheet (GitWriteSheets:218). A re-open renders
  nothing either (the state was already nulled). **NEW ROW F-P40-C (P3)** — the
  refused switch is INDISTINGUISHABLE from success; the F-P0-C silent family on
  the branch plane. Compounding nuance: IssueLine renders the LOCALIZED line by
  code (8 known codes + branch_issue_unknown) and lists paths — the wire's
  `message`/`detail` are decoded but never rendered (the "detail copyable" doc
  comment is unimplemented), so even a fixed face needs the message half. Fix
  shape: keep the sheet open on issues (close only on ok) or render the issue
  card pane-level; render message/detail.
- **MOCK_GIT_REFUSALS=getChanges=fault.git.notAvailable** (fresh process):
  `git.getChanges begin → refused: fault.git.notAvailable` ×2 (both tabs,
  22:55) → the Changes section renders **header → EMPTY → straight to History**
  (s30) — no error, no Retry. Mechanism pinned: the render site EXISTS
  (GitScreen:204 `ui.changesError?.let` + git_changes_error/git_changes_retry)
  but the PORT swallows the refusal first — Phase9Ports.kt:124
  `changes(...) = run("git.changes") {...} ?: emptyList()` (the Channel-refusal
  wrapper maps ANY failure to null) — so fetchChanges's
  `exceptionOrNull()`-based error plumbing never sees a throw and
  changesError stays null. **F-P5-A stamp 2** (the pass-5 row's exact shape —
  "refused git reads render SILENT-EMPTY sections" — now on the live Changes
  tab with the render-site/port mismatch pinned; the fix belongs to the
  port/loader boundary).

   reconnect ladder wedged (TIMEOUT → RECONNECTING, no CONNECTED for 4+ min) — the
   guaranteed recovery (full `adb emu kill` + cold boot `-no-snapshot-load`) restored
   CONNECTED in one ladder cycle. The stored endpoints SURVIVED the reboot (constant
   mock passHash) — no re-pairing, and the persisted prefs (workspaceOrder
   [ws-two, ws-one]) survived too (the chips row re-rendered in the reordered state).

## AS.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The header-tap hazard re-manifested EXACTLY as pass 37 recorded**: tapping the
   conversation header's status capsule opened the CONFIG-CHIPS ROW (mode/followup/
   Effort expanded inline) instead of the SessionContextSheet — the sheet's entry is
   the "Context" CHIP at the header's right (ConversationScreen.kt:742 "the Context
   chip opens SessionContextSheet"). Two taps burned; the chip is the recipe.
2. **A screenshot-sized receipt is NOT always ~1.4 MB-class**: the pass's content
   screens (search results, diff hunks) pulled 110–200 KB PNGs on this swiftshader
   rig — the size heuristic is a BOOT-screen signal, not a per-shot gate (the dump +
   the wire remain the arbiters).
3. **The diff card's toggle target is the HEADER ROW (≥48dp affordance, §30), NOT the
   "Tap to expand" hint text** (DiffRenderer.kt:95-100 — the Row carries the clickable;
   the hint is the collapsed-state label): the first tap at the hint's y did nothing;
   the header-row tap toggled. Re-learned the generic rule: tap the ROW HEADER, not
   its caption.
4. **`run-as … md5sum` on a wildcard /data/app path fails on this image** ("no matches
   found" — the zsh-side glob ate it); the `pm path <pkg>` output pasted literally into
   `adb shell md5sum "<path>"` is the recipe (the pass-33 note's full-path rule,
   now with the quoting form).

## AT.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The launcher hand-write trap re-manifested with a NEW, nastier failure mode**: the
   hand-written heredoc mangled `kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm/1.9.0/` into
   `kotlinx-serialization-core-jvm-1.9.0/` (the version folded into the DIRECTORY
   component — a VALID-LOOKING path that simply doesn't exist) →
   `NoClassDefFoundError: kotlinx/serialization/StringFormat` at relay boot while the
   jar itself was present and healthy. The pass-41 learning ("derive launchers with
   sed — a hand-copied classpath dropped a group-dir segment") re-confirmed with the
   twist that the mangle survives a visual read; the diagnosis was `cmp` on the exec
   lines (byte 753), the fix was deriving the launcher by `head -1`/`tail -1` from the
   KNOWN-WORKING p42 file and writing only the arms/nonce lines fresh. DERIVE, never
   hand-write the classpath.
2. **The IME types THROUGH result-pane swipes**: three `input swipe` drags over the
   open keyboard committed " to to to" into the search field (the drag path crossed
   the space key three times) — the query became "synthetic to to to" → "No tasks
   match." and the pane was lost. Recovery = X-close + re-open + retype. Prevention =
   dismiss the IME BEFORE any swipe, and the only recipe that works is **BACK once
   (keyevent 4) after typing** — keyevent 111 (ESC) does NOT close this IME and the
   keyboard-chevron tap at its visible position missed.
3. **A dump-parse label ate the tap args**: `grep -o '[0-9]*'` over an echo line
   containing "hit-27 tap: 540 1845" pulled the "27" out of the LABEL and the shell
   fed `input tap 540 27`-class garbage (Android "Argument expected after 27").
   Labels in intermediate files must be digit-free, or parse only the numeric tail
   strictly.
4. **The gen1 relaunch wedge** (the pass-27 recipe re-confirmed): after a pkill +
   relay relaunch, the FOREGROUNDED app (same pid) sat silent for 30+s with zero
   connect lines — one force-stop + `am start -W` relaunch connected immediately
   (hello + subscribe on relay-1). The 11s TotalTime cold start is normal for the
   swiftshader rig.

## AU.A0 — rig learnings

1. **A GMS "Sign in — Google Accounts" interstitial hijacks the foreground on this
   long-lived emulator** (twice this pass): the second BACK of a Settings exit-chain
   fell off the app into the system setup nag (`glif_layout`/`minute_maid`), which also
   explains the `UiTestAutomationBridge` "null root node" dump failures at those
   moments. Recovery = SKIP tap (108,2175) + `am start -W` relaunch (the process and
   its in-memory hub state SURVIVE — pid unchanged, the hooks ledger intact). Do NOT
   assume a null-root dump means a crash; screencap + look for `sud_layout_*` ids.
2. **Tapping y-coordinates from a DIFFERENT screen's layout silently navigates
   elsewhere**: the (540,1358) "task row" tap fired while still ON the Settings screen
   opened `settings_mcp` (the MCP row sits at that y) — the conversation-open check
   then saw a stale dump. Always dump-and-verify the CURRENT screen before a
   coordinate tap after any unexpected BACK result.
3. **The mock's respondError answers are invisible in the relay log** (only
   `MOCK: command type=…` and v4call lines print; the error response itself is silent)
   — the OUTBOX's `ackReasonCode` is the typed-fault arbiter
   (`fault.command.rigRefused:requestWorkspaceHookReview` rode the DB row verbatim).
4. The `sqlite3` WAL dance: query the PULLED `zcode.db` with its `-wal` sibling in

   channel calls printed NOTHING before it (the `MOCK: v4call` lines cover only the
   JSON-RPC layer), so `restoreBetweenCheckpoints`' from/to ids were invisible — the
   F-P45-A divergence is arg-exact BECAUSE of the rig fix. Precedent for future

   bounds matched the screenshot estimate within ~40px; the ~200px lie did not
   manifest on this dialog class) — but the screenshot cross-check stays mandatory.

   (the sheet dump caught the context sheet — the Git tap fired pre-render). One

## AV.E — Leg D: the FORCE-PAIR DIVERGENCE — NEW ROW F-P45-A (P2)

The 3-checkpoint divergence leg: list [ckpt-3, ckpt-2, ckpt-1], tap Restore on the
MIDDLE row (ckpt-2's) → confirm reads **"to snapshot ckpt-1 (from ckpt-3)"** → the
wire carries `{fromCheckpointId:"ckpt-1","toCheckpointId":"ckpt-3"}` → conflict face
→ Overwrite → **the wire carries `{fromCheckpointId:"ckpt-2","toCheckpointId":
"ckpt-3","force":true}`** — THE `fromCheckpointId` CHANGED under the force. The user
confirmed restoring the workspace to ckpt-1 and the destructive overwrite executed
against ckpt-2 (one generation newer — silently KEEPING the changes the user asked
to discard). Mechanism (`GitScreen.kt` CheckpointsCard): `forceConfirmFor` carries
only `(to, conflicts)` and the force handler RECOMPUTES `from = checkpoints
.getOrNull(1)` — a hard-coded index that happens to match the confirmed pair only
when the list has exactly two entries (Leg C looked correct BECAUSE of that
coincidence). Trigger: ≥3 checkpoints + a conflict (the common case on a dirty
worktree — the reason the conflict face exists) + Overwrite. **Adjudication: NEW ROW
F-P45-A (P2)** — a destructive ⚠-surface write diverging from its own confirmation,
the F-P40-C confirm-then-different-execution family at destructive severity. Fix
shape: carry the confirmed `from` through `forceConfirmFor` (Triple or a data pair);
pin: a compose harness with a 3-item list asserting the force wire ids == the
confirmed pair.

## AX.A0 — rig learnings

1. **The terminal search typing leg did NOT trip the F-P0-E ANR** (one 5-char `input
   text` + one IME dismiss) — the trajectory sheet's ZERO-typing budget stays the
   safe rule, but ordinary short single-field typing on this rig remains viable.
2. **Stale singleton-port state survives navigation**: the terminal controller is a
   screen-independent singleton — a CapabilityOff (or Live/Exited) state re-renders
   on every re-entry until something calls detach (state→Idle) or the capability
   gate re-runs. The CapabilityOff branch offers NO recovery affordance at all — the
   receipted escape is the SETTINGS opt-in toggle OFF→ON (setOptIn(false) → detach →
   Idle). Budget for it when driving cap-off arms: the Settings path (screen row →
   repository.update — which BYPASSES DefaultTerminalPort.setOptIn's terminal.optIn
   log line; the dump's checked state + the pb bytes are the arbiter, not logcat).
3. **Chip-row bounds shift when a label flips** ("Copy visible output" → "Copied"
   slides Detach left ~200 px) — the dialog-tap rule (screenshot-derived bounds)
   applies to ASSIST CHIPS too: dump AFTER the flip, never reuse stale bounds.
4. The `MOCK: terminal create` arg line receipts the grid the controller offers:
   `{"cols":120,"rows":32}` ×3, NO `cwd` key — the ADR-022 "create with a custom cwd"
   never-ported hold, live-verified.
5. uiautomator null-root during route transitions persists (the d25 dump caught the
   sheet-dismiss frame: header-only, body empty; the settle-retry d26 showed the true
   state). Screenshots remain ground truth on busy frames.

## Binding rules for every fix session

1. **Repo + branch.** Work in this repo on `fix/pass0` cut from `main`. Every fix round commits
   locally as `ErnestHysa <takis312@hotmail.com>` (set repo-locally BEFORE the first commit);
   **never push unless Ernest says.**
2. **One finding ≥ one commit**, message `fix(<ID>): <mechanism>`. One commit may close several
   rows ONLY when they are one shared mechanism (rule 10) — name every covered ID and tick them all.
   Never bundle unrelated rows to "save a suite run".
3. **Re-read before fixing.** Re-read the row's ledger entry and its Part citations before
   writing code; honor the row's named re-scopes (e.g. F-P45-B's sink key, F-P40-B's
   rename-only scope, F-P13-A's stay-open boundary which is HEALTHY and must stay so).
4. **TEST-FIRST with shape fidelity.** The pin named in the row (every row carries one) is
   written and RED at the pre-fix commit.
5. **Every fix ships its pin in the same commit.** Mock/rig changes are separate `fix(mock)`
   commits with `:tools:mockzcode:jar` + `:tools:mockzcode:test` green; a mock change never
   closes an app row.
6. **COMMIT BEFORE ANY TEST OR RIG RUN.** No uncommitted edits anywhere in the repo while any
   gradle pool or emulator runs (the standing reversion hazard). Rig hygiene per the ledger's
   STEP RIG: `pkill -f MockRelayMainKt` never by port; restart `adb logcat -T 1` after every
   emulator restart; absent log lines are inconclusive — the DB pull arbitrates.
7. **Fresh full-suite baseline + zero-new-names gate.** `testDebugUnitTest` for the Android
   modules AND `test` for the six pure-JVM modules (a name-diff missing those six is blind to a
   third of the repo). After each fix re-run the touched modules; name-diff every new failing
   name against the pre-phase baseline; ALSO assert the gradle task-failure list holds only
   test-failure tasks and every module emitted test XML (a test-compile failure is invisible to
   a name-diff).
8. **~150-line / stop rule.** A change beyond ~150 lines or spanning >3 modules stops for a
   checkpoint commit + suite re-run.
9. **Independent per-phase verification.** A phase is done only when its exit gate passes on a
   FRESH emulator+relay rig leg (zcode-a16 cold boot `-no-snapshot-load`, the standing arming
   plus the phase's named arms, wire receipts appended to this report, rows ticked). A docs-only
   or pin-only close never satisfies an Accept criterion that names a wire/DB arbiter.
10. **Shared-remedy preference.** The named families: F-P0-B unblocks F-P6-A (card half);
    F-P8-D unblocks F-P6-B; **F-P19-A + F-P20-A are ONE pair** (the same held-queue guard
    family); the **N-BR-1/N-BS-1/N-BT-1 notice one-liners batch** into one sub-phase (N-BO-1
    rides the same notice plane); F-P13-A and F-P48-A share the CONNECTED-transition surface
    (Phase 9 consumes Phase 1's hook); **G102 carries F-P39-A's move-copy fix**.
11. **Record duty.** Tick rows here as their Accept criteria pass; re-status the ledger row
    FIXED with the commit sha; append a dated fix-round record at the file end; keep the
    one-report-file append-only discipline.

## Phase 1 — Connection, recovery & transport state

Theme: the endpoint/recovery plane that every other surface rides on. Order inside the phase:
**F-P8-A → F-P9-A → F-P9-B → F-P13-A → F-P8-B → K-small-2.**

### Sub-phase 1A — endpoint persistence & wedges

- [x] **F-P8-A (P2) — cold start with DIRECT selected: the deferred relay `persistEndpoint`
  rewrites `_endpoint` after resolve, silently abandoning the resolved selection.**
  `ConnectionHub.kt:672-685 → :1650` re-persists post-resolve; the recovery is dropped by the
  `sourceKind` filter; the UI shows "First sync failed" beside a healthy direct endpoint; Retry
  completes it. **Fix:** guard `persistEndpoint` against overwriting a resolved non-relay
  selection; retry must reconnect the transport the UI shows. **Accept:** a Robolectric race pin
  + a "no `hub.switched` without user tap" assert; a live cold-start DIRECT leg renders the
  healthy direct face with no false failed strip. (F-P2-A's supersession: the REAL root is
  here.)
- [x] **F-P9-A (P2) — relay killed MID-AUTHENTICATION wedges the transport in AUTHENTICATING
  permanently** (zero sockets, zero ladder, zero logs, 8 min receipted; survives
  foreground/unlock; NO retry face — cached rows suppress the strip; the active-endpoint tap is
  a silent no-op; only escape = a cross-endpoint switch away+back). Three trigger variants
  receipted (pass 9 mid-auth, pass 10 stale-relay, pass 15 relay-absent cold start → 10 s
  timeout). **Fix:** an AUTHENTICATING watchdog (timeout → RECOVERING) + a stuck face.
  **Accept:** a Robolectric kill-mid-handshake pin (netstat-zero + "no silent state" assert); a
  live leg kills the relay at handshake → the face flips within the timeout and Retry
  reconnects.
- [x] **F-P9-B (P2) — the typed disconnected-remote face never renders live:** the hub logs
  `workspace-bridge-error: remote-disconnected` but ConnectionCenter shows the generic offline
  face — the G67 card (`connection_remote_reconnect`, render condition
  `lastError.messageKey==REMOTE_WORKSPACE_DISCONNECTED`, `ConnectionCenterScreen.kt:296`) never
  renders → the recovery verb workspace-reconnect-request is UI-unreachable. **Fix:** trace
  `hub.connectFailed → lastError` dropping the messageKey (the SESSION-scope bridge error).
  **Accept:** a live-shape harness asserting the card renders with the arm armed; the
  workspace-reconnect verb reachable from the card.

### Sub-phase 1B — recovery, reconnection state & the sync strip

- [x] **F-P13-A (P2) — the workflowRun delta plane is DEAD on the CLOSE-CYCLE post-recovery
  path:** the detach path drops the local subscription record (`recovery.detached` — detach()
  fires only from closeConversation, `ConnectionHub.kt:1027-1052` →
  `RecoveryCoordinator.kt:130-149`), the recovery re-materializes conversations via
  `relay.recovered :: subscriptions=N` issuing NO subscribeConversationV4, so the subscribe-ACK
  epoch record is never re-stamped → EVERY server-initiated delta drops at
  `ConversationGateway.kt:261-274` (`gateway.drop … no subscription record`) for the life of
  the connection. The STAY-OPEN path is HEALTHY (pass 15) and must stay so. **Fix:** recovery
  must re-subscribe (or stamp epochs on the snapshotReplace ack) ON THE DETACHED-REOPEN path.
  **Accept:** a relay-log pin ("no subscribe after recovered") + a gateway.drop assert on a
  post-close-cycle delta; a live leg applies deltas with seq > 1 and zero gateway.drop; the
  stay-open boundary re-receipted. (The patch variant is stamped pass 44 — same gateway, same
  fix.)
- [x] **F-P8-B (P3) — switching to an already-CONNECTED endpoint throws ISE `connect() is the
  first-connection path`.** **Fix:** `connectDirect()` → `recover()`/no-op when
  state==CONNECTED. **Accept:** a harness asserting a second tap on the connected endpoint does

- [x] **K-small-2 (P4) — "First sync failed" renders alongside CACHED rows** (wording/state

  transport ~1 s after attach (TRIGGER CLOSED pass 49 — FRAME-COUNT class, the phone reader:
  the 2400-frame `big` arm dropped at ~6-26 frames paced AND unpaced; `bigone`'s identical
  525.6 KB in ONE frame held; the `big` arm is the pin-harness stream shape, `bigone` the

  — the recovery affordance is an invisible/unlabeled pill (it WORKS; TalkBack hears nothing).
  The Idle branch passes `retryLabel = terminal_attach` correctly; the CapabilityOff branch
